subtitle: damnit, whole thing turns on where you stand
body: It seems like, standing here, above all, perspective is what truly matters...or how to look at it, at least..., luckily we can find some clues in projective geometry.

steps.text: Let's draw a line with three points on it.
Let's draw a second parallel line with three points on it.
Look closely, we can connect every point to its corresponding point and see that each of those connecting lines passes through the same point, which we can call the perspectivity point.

closing: So let's define perspectivity more formally.

Two sets of points $A_1, A_2, A_3$ and $B_1, B_2, B_3$ are perspective to one another with respect to a point $P$, when the sets can be put into one-to-one correspondence, so that any two corresponding points are joined by a line through $P$.
Point $P$ acts as the central viewpoint, which unites the two separate lines ($a$ and $b$) into a single correlated system.
